1	# Prover records
2	
3	This directory holds one record per review pass. Every push carries exactly one of them, and that
4	one record does the whole job: it is the fresh re-check of `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`
5	that the push gate has always demanded, and it is the adversarial read of the change the push is
6	about to send. The reviewer is briefed to find reasons the change should be refused, and holds the
7	change defective until evidence says otherwise. A read that sets out to confirm the change leaves
8	the requirement unmet.
9	
10	The rule lives in `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` under `[M-6]`, `[INV-116]` and `[INV-304]`. The gate that reads
11	these records is `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh`, wired into `guardrails/pre-push` as gate a.
12	
13	Records of review passes that no push carries — a milestone re-prove, a periodic audit — live here
14	too, under the same file naming. Only a record written for a push owes the range fields below.
15	
16	## What the review covers
17	
18	The spec and the architecture as they now stand, and the delta being pushed: every commit between
19	the remote's head and the local head. Whatever is still uncommitted is read with them. The range
20	comes from the base ladder the gate walks — `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE`, then `origin/main`, then `HEAD~1`.
21	
22	The commit list for the record:
23	
24	```
25	git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD
26	```
27	
28	## The record's shape
29	
30	One file per pass, named `YYYY-MM-DD[-slug].md`, committed before the push. The suffix is mandatory
31	once the date's plain file exists.
32	
33	```
34	# Prover record — 2026-08-05 <slug>
35	
36	PUSH-REVIEW
37	
38	Range: 258d544..9f21ab0
39	- 9f21ab0 <subject>
40	- 258d544 <subject>
41	Files read: PRODUCT_SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, guardrails/pre-push
42	Checks run: python3 -m pytest -q — 2,484 passed
43	Findings: <what the review found>
44	Blocking: none
45	```
46	
47	Those are all the fields, and the gate reads every one of them. Each carries a value. The commits
48	between the base and the head are listed under `Range:`, since the gate holds that the record names
49	every commit it covers. A review that found nothing writes into `Findings:` what it examined; the
50	absence then rests on the coverage the fields above state, rather than on silence.
51	
52	`Blocking:` reads `none`, or lists one item per blocking finding. Each item carries `closed:` with
53	what changed, or `stands:` with the reason it stands. A blocking finding holds the push until one of
54	those two is written.
55	
56	## What the gate holds, and what it leaves to the reviewer
57	
58	The gate holds:
59	
60	- a record dated today exists;
61	- the record is committed, rather than a scratch file in the working tree;
62	- the record is no older than the last change to `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` or `ARCHITECTURE.md`;
63	- the record is fresh against the pushed range;
64	- the record names the base commit and every reviewed commit;
65	- each field carries a value, and a blocking finding is closed or explained.
66	
67	The gate leaves three things to the reviewer:
68	
69	- whether the review was adversarial;
70	- whether the files the record names were read;
71	- whether the findings are the ones the delta deserved.
72	
73	No script decides those three. The record's named commits, files, checks and findings are the
74	pressure a machine can apply toward the review being real.

Files read: PRODUCT_SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, guardrails/pre-push
Checks run: python3 -m pytest -q — 2,484 passed
Findings: <what the review found>
Blocking: none
```

Those are all the fields, and the gate reads every one of them. Each carries a value. The commits
between the base and the head are listed under `Range:`, since the gate holds that the record names
every commit it covers. A review that found nothing writes into `Findings:` what it examined; the
absence then rests on the coverage the fields above state, rather than on silence.

`Blocking:` reads `none`, or lists one item per blocking finding. Each item carries `closed:` with
what changed, or `stands:` with the reason it stands. A blocking finding holds the push until one of
those two is written.

## What the gate holds, and what it leaves to the reviewer

The gate holds:

- a record dated today exists;
- the record is committed, rather than a scratch file in the working tree;
- the record is no older than the last change to `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` or `ARCHITECTURE.md`;
- the record is fresh against the pushed range;
- the record names the base commit and every reviewed commit;
- each field carries a value, and a blocking finding is closed or explained.

The gate leaves three things to the reviewer:

- whether the review was adversarial;
- whether the files the record names were read;
- whether the findings are the ones the delta deserved.

No script decides those three. The record's named commits, files, checks and findings are the
pressure a machine can apply toward the review being real.

content.content:
real current state before designing anything on it. It is the resume-side twin of rule 13's primary
   source and of the architecture step's pin read from a command just run. Rule 8 re-reads versions at a
   breakpoint, and the queue-take re-scan re-reads a deferred row's revisit trigger [SPEC INV-129].
   This rule re-reads the item's own internals. So
   a session never designs a fix from a stale model of code that has since moved. And an item already
   handled is caught before the work restarts. The owner asked the pack to hold it, 2026-07-20.

35. **A session's record is read at both ends by an agent that did not live it (SPEC INV-302).** A session
   that lived the work reads its own record badly. Worked failure: on 2026-07-28 a session wrote its
   handover from memory. It named a question as still waiting for the owner, and the owner had answered
   it earlier that day. So each
   end of a session is read by a fresh agent. That agent works from a session extract: the person's own
   turns, each with its timestamp. `scripts/session-extract.py` pulls those turns out of one transcript,
   and its own header names where the transcripts sit and which traps a reader meets there.
   The extract goes to a scratch directory, since a transcript holds private conversation. At the close,
   the fresh agent writes the session handover from that extract. The session that lived the work writes
   no handover of its own. A handover is a file under `docs/handovers/` whose name ends in
   `-handover.md`. It says where it was read from in three lines: transcript, extract, written by.
   At the open, a fresh agent reads the previous session's extract. It lists every decision the person
   made, each with its timestamp. It compares that list against `DECISIONS.md` and `NEXT_STEPS.md`. A
   decision missing from both goes to the seat before work starts.
   Both ends stay a discipline the seat holds. A script read the handover's three lines until
   2026-08-09, and the live-spec pack withdrew that script after finding no error the script had
   ever caught.
   A session's opening writes no committed artifact for a script to read. The owner asked for
   this reading as a standing process, 2026-07-28.

36. **A command that can raise a system dialog announces itself first (SPEC INV-317).** A session
   cannot see a macOS permission dialog — a keychain read, a browser binary's first launch on this
   machine, a camera or a sandbox-guarded folder. It only sees the call block, or a secret return
   empty. Worked failure: one session ran a deploy script reading a Cloudflare key from the keychain,
   then launched a Chrome binary four times, none run on that machine before; the owner met four
   dialogs with no word from the session first and pressed Deny each time, correctly, since an
   unexplained request for a secret has one safe reading. Before running a command known to raise
   one, say so in one line and let the human decide; where the dialog is a standing cost of a

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# adopt/install-ratchet.sh — the turnkey ratchet-adoption kit (SPEC INV-172).
3	#
4	# Run from a HOST repo root. Vendors the pack's style/redundancy/freeze gates and the three pre-show
5	# lints (SPEC INV-316) into the host, seeds a
6	# debt cap at the host's CURRENT size (an adoption run never blocks on pre-existing debt — only on
7	# growth beyond it), and generates a lock test that only ever tightens: doc growth beyond the seeded
8	# cap reds the suite, and raising the cap itself means editing the generated test (deliberate,
9	# visible, reviewed — never a silent raise).
10	#
11	# Usage: adopt/install-ratchet.sh [--force] [--tier universal|full] [DOC ...]
12	#   DOC...     gated doc paths (relative to the host root). If omitted: read
13	#              guardrails.config.json's spec_path (+ extra_gated_docs) if present in the host root,
14	#              else default to PRODUCT_SPEC.md if that file exists, else fail.
15	#   --force    overwrite an already-vendored file (default: skip an existing file and note it).
16	#   --tier     tier passed to the vendored style lint when seeding + locking (default: universal).
17	set -euo pipefail
18	
19	PACK_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
20	HOST_ROOT="$(pwd)"
21	
22	FORCE=0
23	TIER="universal"
24	DOCS=()
25	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
26	  case "$1" in
27	    --force) FORCE=1; shift ;;
28	    --tier) TIER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
29	    --tier=*) TIER="${1#--tier=}"; shift ;;
30	    *) DOCS+=("$1"); shift ;;
31	  esac
32	done
33	
34	# --- step a: resolve the host's gated doc set --------------------------------------------------
35	if [ ${#DOCS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
36	  if [ -f "$HOST_ROOT/guardrails.config.json" ]; then
37	    while IFS= read -r d; do
38	      [ -n "$d" ] && DOCS+=("$d")
39	    done < <(python3 - "$HOST_ROOT/guardrails.config.json" << 'PYEOF'
40	import json, sys
41	cfg = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
42	docs = []
43	if cfg.get("spec_path"):
44	    docs.append(cfg["spec_path"])
45	docs.extend(cfg.get("extra_gated_docs") or [])
46	for d in docs:
47	    print(d)
48	PYEOF
49	)
50	  elif [ -f "$HOST_ROOT/PRODUCT_SPEC.md" ]; then
51	    DOCS=("PRODUCT_SPEC.md")
52	  fi
53	fi
54	
55	if [ ${#DOCS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
56	  echo '{"severity":"error","code":"ratchet-install","message":"no gated docs found","fix":"pass doc paths as arguments"}'
57	  exit 1
58	fi
59	
60	# --- step b: vendor the pack's gate files into the host ------------------------------------------
61	VENDOR_FILES=(
62	  "scripts/spec-style-lint.py"
63	  "scripts/spec-style-lint.json"
64	  "scripts/spec-redundancy-precheck.py"
65	  "scripts/spec-freeze.py"
66	  "scripts/spec-freeze.json"
67	  "scripts/gate_common.py"
68	  "guardrails/check-freeze.sh"
69	  "guardrails/spec-coinages.json"
70	  "scripts/preshow-lint.py"
71	  "scripts/preshow-register-lint.py"
72	  "scripts/preshow-legibility-lint.py"
73	)
74	
75	for rel in "${VENDOR_FILES[@]}"; do
76	  src="$PACK_ROOT/$rel"
77	  dest="$HOST_ROOT/$rel"
78	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
79	  if [ -f "$dest" ] && [ "$FORCE" -ne 1 ]; then
80	    echo "skip (exists, use --force to overwrite): $rel"
81	  else
82	    cp "$src" "$dest"
83	    echo "vendored: $rel"
84	  fi
85	done
86	
87	# --- step d: seed caps at the host's CURRENT size -----------------------------------------------
88	STYLE_ERRORS=0
89	REDUNDANCY_OPEN=0
90	for doc in "${DOCS[@]}"; do
91	  style_out="$(python3 "$HOST_ROOT/scripts/spec-style-lint.py" --tier "$TIER" "$HOST_ROOT/$doc" 2>&1 || true)"
92	  style_json="$(printf '%s\n' "$style_out" | tail -n1)"
93	  n="$(python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.argv[1])['errors'])" "$style_json")"
94	  STYLE_ERRORS=$((STYLE_ERRORS + n))
95	
96	  redundancy_out="$(python3 "$HOST_ROOT/scripts/spec-redundancy-precheck.py" "$HOST_ROOT/$doc" 2>&1 || true)"
97	  redundancy_json="$(printf '%s\n' "$redundancy_out" | tail -n1)"
98	  m="$(python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.argv[1])['open'])" "$redundancy_json")"
99	  REDUNDANCY_OPEN=$((REDUNDANCY_OPEN + m))
100	done
101	
102	# --- step c + d: write the manifest, the debt cap, and the generated lock test -------------------
103	python3 - "$HOST_ROOT" "$PACK_ROOT" "$TIER" "$STYLE_ERRORS" "$REDUNDANCY_OPEN" "${DOCS[@]}" << 'PYEOF'
104	import hashlib
105	import json
106	import os
107	import sys
108	
109	host_root, pack_root, tier = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
110	style_errors, redundancy_open = int(sys.argv[4]), int(sys.argv[5])
111	docs = sys.argv[6:]
112	
113	# Kept in step with the VENDOR_FILES shell array above by hand: this list is what the update
114	# watcher pins, so a file vendored there and missing here changes in the pack without the host
115	# hearing of it. A data file counts as much as its script — a lint whose word list moved is a
116	# different lint.
117	VENDOR_FILES = [
118	    "scripts/spec-style-lint.py",
119	    "scripts/spec-style-lint.json",
120	    "scripts/spec-redundancy-precheck.py",
121	    "scripts/spec-freeze.py",
122	    "scripts/spec-freeze.json",
123	    "scripts/gate_common.py",
124	    "guardrails/check-freeze.sh",
125	    "guardrails/spec-coinages.json",
126	    "scripts/preshow-lint.py",
127	    "scripts/preshow-register-lint.py",
128	    "scripts/preshow-legibility-lint.py",
129	]
130	
131	
132	def sha256_of(path):
133	    h = hashlib.sha256()
134	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
135	        h.update(f.read())
136	    return h.hexdigest()
137	
138	
139	pack_version = open(os.path.join(pack_root, "VERSION"), encoding="utf-8").read().strip()
140	
141	scripts_dir = os.path.join(host_root, "scripts")
142	tests_dir = os.path.join(host_root, "tests")
143	os.makedirs(scripts_dir, exist_ok=True)
144	os.makedirs(tests_dir, exist_ok=True)
145	
146	# The manifest is MERGED, never rebuilt from scratch: a scaffold install (adopt/install-scaffold.sh)
147	# may already have pinned its checks here, and a fresh ratchet run must not drop those keys (the
148	# 2026-07-16 defect — a from-scratch rebuild silently dropped a prior scaffold install's keys). Read
149	# whatever manifest exists, update only this installer's own entries, and leave every other prior
150	# entry — scaffold's pack-relative keys included — exactly as found.
151	manifest_path = os.path.join(scripts_dir, "ratchet-manifest.json")
152	manifest = {"pack_version": pack_version, "vendored": {}}
153	if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
154	    try:
155	        manifest = json.load(open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8"))
156	    except (OSError, ValueError):
157	        manifest = {"pack_version": pack_version, "vendored": {}}
158	vendored = manifest.setdefault("vendored", {})
159	
160	# The scaffold kit's files, where the host carries them, join the manifest (the design-review
161	# recommendation of 2026-07-16: one source-pin mechanism covers both installable kits, so the
162	# update watcher reads one file). Informational pins; this installer never vendors them.
163	SCAFFOLD_NAMES = ("check_completeness.py", "check_tests_present.py",
164	                  "check_traces_to_spec.py", "check_conflicts.py", "gate_lib.py")
165	
166	# Dedupe first: a host-relative guardrails/<name> pin never resolves against the pack (only the
167	# pack-relative scaffold/guardrails/<name> form does) — drop either dir form of a prior scaffold-check
168	# key before re-pinning, mirroring install-scaffold.sh's own dedupe, so a host that hit the old
169	# opportunistic host-relative pin gets it cleaned up here too.
170	for key in list(vendored):
171	    base = os.path.basename(key)
172	    d = os.path.dirname(key)
173	    if base in SCAFFOLD_NAMES and d in ("guardrails", "scaffold/guardrails"):
174	        del vendored[key]
175	
176	# This installer's own vendored set is always current.
177	for rel in VENDOR_FILES:
178	    vendored[rel] = sha256_of(os.path.join(host_root, rel))
179	
180	# Re-derive scaffold pins from whatever the host actually carries, always under the pack-relative
181	# key so the watcher resolves it against the pack checkout, never a host path.
182	for name in SCAFFOLD_NAMES:
183	    for d in ("scaffold/guardrails", "guardrails"):
184	        p = os.path.join(host_root, d, name)
185	        if os.path.isfile(p):
186	            vendored["scaffold/guardrails/%s" % name] = sha256_of(p)
187	            break
188	
189	manifest["pack_version"] = pack_version
190	manifest["seeded"] = {"style_errors": style_errors, "redundancy_open": redundancy_open}
191	manifest["tier"] = tier
192	
193	with open(manifest_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
194	    json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)
195	    f.write("\n")
196	print("wrote scripts/ratchet-manifest.json")
197	
198	cap = {"max_waivers": 0, "max_redundancy_open": redundancy_open, "max_style_errors": style_errors}
199	with open(os.path.join(scripts_dir, "spec-debt-cap.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
200	    json.dump(cap, f, indent=2)
201	    f.write("\n")
202	print("wrote scripts/spec-debt-cap.json (max_style_errors=%d max_redundancy_open=%d)"
203	      % (style_errors, redundancy_open))
204	
205	LOCK_TEST_TEMPLATE = '''"""tests/test_ratchet_lock.py — generated by adopt/install-ratchet.sh (SPEC INV-172). Do not hand-edit
206	the SEEDED_* constants; they are the size measured at adoption time. The ratchet only ever tightens:
207	the suite reds when a gated doc grows past the seeded size, and reds when scripts/spec-debt-cap.json
208	is raised past what was seeded here — raising a cap for real means editing this file, on purpose,
209	reviewed.
210	"""
211	import json
212	import os
213	import subprocess
214	
215	SEEDED_STYLE_ERRORS = {seeded_style_errors}
216	SEEDED_REDUNDANCY_OPEN = {seeded_redundancy_open}
217	GATED_DOCS = {gated_docs!r}
218	TIER = {tier!r}

#
# Run from a HOST repo root. Vendors the pack's style/redundancy/freeze gates and the three pre-show
# lints (SPEC INV-316) into the host, seeds a
# debt cap at the host's CURRENT size (an adoption run never blocks on pre-existing debt — only on
# growth beyond it), and generates a lock test that only ever tightens: doc growth beyond the seeded
# cap reds the suite, and raising the cap itself means editing the generated test (deliberate,
# visible, reviewed — never a silent raise).
#

#   DOC...     gated doc paths (relative to the host root). If omitted: read
#              guardrails.config.json's spec_path (+ extra_gated_docs) if present in the host root,
#              else default to PRODUCT_SPEC.md if that file exists, else fail.
#   --force    overwrite an already-vendored file (default: skip an existing file and note it).
#   --tier     tier passed to the vendored style lint when seeding + locking (default: universal).
set -euo pipefail

PACK_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
HOST_ROOT="$(pwd)"

FORCE=0
TIER="universal"
DOCS=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --force) FORCE=1; shift ;;
    --tier) TIER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --tier=*) TIER="${1#--tier=}"; shift ;;
    *) DOCS+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done

    while IFS= read -r d; do

if cfg.get("spec_path"):
    docs.append(cfg["spec_path"])
docs.extend(cfg.get("extra_gated_docs") or [])
for d in docs:
    print(d)
PYEOF
)
  elif [ -f "$HOST_ROOT/PRODUCT_SPEC.md" ]; then
    DOCS=("PRODUCT_SPEC.md")
  fi
fi

  "scripts/spec-style-lint.py"
  "scripts/spec-style-lint.json"
  "scripts/spec-redundancy-precheck.py"
  "scripts/spec-freeze.py"
  "scripts/spec-freeze.json"
  "scripts/gate_common.py"
  "guardrails/check-freeze.sh"
  "guardrails/spec-coinages.json"
  "scripts/preshow-lint.py"
  "scripts/preshow-register-lint.py"
  "scripts/preshow-legibility-lint.py"
)

  src="$PACK_ROOT/$rel"

  redundancy_json="$(printf '%s\n' "$redundancy_out" | tail -n1)"

    """Return (kind, index): index to insert BEFORE ('fail_check'/'trailing_exit'), 'append' means
    at end (index == len(lines)), 'ambiguous' means no safe anchor was found (index is None)."""
    fail_idx = None
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if FAIL_CHECK_RE.match(line.strip()):
            fail_idx = i  # keep the LAST match
    if fail_idx is not None:
        return ("fail_check", fail_idx)

    last_i = len(lines) - 1
    while last_i >= 0 and lines[last_i].strip() == "":
        last_i -= 1
    if last_i >= 0 and TOPLEVEL_EXIT_RE.match(lines[last_i]):
        return ("trailing_exit", last_i)

    for line in lines:
        if TOPLEVEL_EXIT_RE.match(line):
            return ("ambiguous", None)

    return ("append", len(lines))


def insert_at(lines, kind, idx):
    if kind == "append":
        return lines + BLOCK_LINES
    return lines[:idx] + BLOCK_LINES + lines[idx:]

    lines = read_lines(path)
    existing = find_existing(lines)

    if existing is not None:
        start, end = block_bounds(lines, existing)
        dead = any(TOPLEVEL_EXIT_RE.match(lines[i]) for i in range(start))

            print("already-wired")
            sys.exit(0)
        stripped = lines[:start] + lines[end:]
        kind, idx = find_anchor(stripped)
        if kind == "ambiguous":
            print("manual")
            sys.exit(0)
        write_lines(path, insert_at(stripped, kind, idx))
        print("repaired")
        sys.exit(0)

    kind, idx = find_anchor(lines)
    if kind == "ambiguous":
        print("manual")
        sys.exit(0)
    write_lines(path, insert_at(lines, kind, idx))
    print("wired")

    print("manual")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install.sh — copies live-spec skills into ~/.claude/skills/
# Idempotent: backs up any existing skill with a timestamp before overwriting.
# Usage: ./install.sh

set -euo pipefail

SKILLS_SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/skills" && pwd)"
SKILLS_DEST="$HOME/.claude/skills"
TIMESTAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"

mkdir -p "$SKILLS_DEST"  # a fresh machine has no skills home yet (E-21's fresh-install promise)

echo "live-spec install — copying skills to $SKILLS_DEST"
echo "Timestamp for backups: $TIMESTAMP"
echo ""

for skill_dir in "$SKILLS_SRC"/*/; do
  skill_name="$(basename "$skill_dir")"
  if [ -e "$skill_dir/.git" ]; then
    echo "  $skill_name — SKIPPED (external skill's canonical clone; scripts/install-external-skills.sh owns it)"
    continue
  fi
  dest="$SKILLS_DEST/$skill_name"

  if [ -d "$dest" ]; then
    backup_home="$SKILLS_DEST-attic"
    mkdir -p "$backup_home"
    backup="$backup_home/$skill_name.bak_$TIMESTAMP"
    echo "  $skill_name — backing up existing to $backup"
    cp -r "$dest" "$backup"
  else
    echo "  $skill_name — new install"
  fi

  cp -r "$skill_dir" "$dest"
  echo "  $skill_name — installed"
done

echo ""
echo "Done. Skills available in ~/.claude/skills/:"
ls "$SKILLS_DEST"

        "scripts/spec-style-lint.py",
        "scripts/spec-redundancy-precheck.py",
        "scripts/spec-freeze.py",
        "scripts/gate_common.py",
        "guardrails/check-freeze.sh",
        "scripts/preshow-lint.py",
        "scripts/preshow-register-lint.py",
        "scripts/preshow-legibility-lint.py",
    )

    def _init_host(self, tmp):
        run(["git", "init", "-q"], cwd=tmp)
        run(["git", "config", "user.email", "a@example.com"], cwd=tmp)
        run(["git", "config", "user.name", "a"], cwd=tmp)

    def _measured_style_errors(self, doc_path):
        result = run(["python3", os.path.join(ROOT, "scripts", "spec-style-lint.py"),
                       "--tier", "universal", doc_path])
        last_line = result.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1]
        return json.loads(last_line)["errors"]

    def _write_doc(self, tmp):
        doc = os.path.join(tmp, "DOC.md")
        with open(doc, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(
                "# Test doc\n\n"
                "The output is good — not bad quality.\n\n"
                "The result is good — not bad quality.\n"
            )
        return doc

    def test_ratchet_install_seeds_at_current_size(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            self._init_host(tmp)
            doc = self._write_doc(tmp)
            expected = self._measured_style_errors(doc)
            self.assertGreater(expected, 0, "fixture doc must trip at least one style error")

            result = run(["bash", INSTALL_RATCHET, "DOC.md"], cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout + result.stderr)

            for rel in self.VENDOR_FILES:
                self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(tmp, rel)), "missing vendored: %s" % rel)

            manifest_path = os.path.join(tmp, "scripts", "ratchet-manifest.json")
            self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(manifest_path))
            manifest = json.load(open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8"))
            pack_version = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "VERSION"), encoding="utf-8").read().strip()
            self.assertEqual(manifest["pack_version"], pack_version)
            for rel in self.VENDOR_FILES:
                actual_sha = hashlib.sha256(open(os.path.join(tmp, rel), "rb").read()).hexdigest()
                self.assertEqual(manifest["vendored"][rel], actual_sha)

            cap_path = os.path.join(tmp, "scripts", "spec-debt-cap.json")
            self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(cap_path))
            cap = json.load(open(cap_path, encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertEqual(cap["max_style_errors"], expected)

            lock_test = os.path.join(tmp, "tests", "test_ratchet_lock.py")
            self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(lock_test))

            result2 = run(["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "tests/test_ratchet_lock.py"], cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual(result2.returncode, 0, result2.stdout + result2.stderr)

    def test_ratchet_lock_reds_on_growth(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            self._init_host(tmp)
            doc = self._write_doc(tmp)

      example when the tests are running locally)** — the heartbeat's forward-looking face. When the
      coming stretch needs nothing from the human, say so before it starts. Such a stretch is a local
      suite run, a worker batch, or a long render. Say three things: that he may step away, an honest
      range for how long, and what he is needed for at its end. Read the range from the work's known
      shape or observed runs; unknown is said as unknown, and a guess is never dressed as a promise.
      When he is needed again, that is a beat too — a chat line awaiting his return, never a summons.
      Reaching an absent human is outside this rule. The window is a read on the work, never a dismissal.
      Beats keep landing during it, so the returning reader finds the trail whole. Questions born inside
      it batch to its end (base rule 1). A window that ends off its spoken range says so — overrun, done
      sooner, or blocked on his word alone. And no offline sentence fires when the very next beat needs the human.

      that says the machine is about to close or sleep), the session stops taking new work. It walks
      what is open to a shutdown-safe stop, on four counts. Background workers are halted or run to
      their landing, since a sleeping machine kills them mid-write (SPEC INV-76). One that cannot halt
      in time is recorded by the handoff discipline, and its death-with-sleep is said aloud. Every open
      lane stands at its checkpoint (base rule 6). Red work is never committed: the failing test name
      and hypothesis top the resume file. Green work is committed under its standing gates. The resume
      file says what resumes where. The walk's first beat answers in minutes: roughly how long to the
      safe point (SPEC INV-93). Its last is one closing line — safe to power off, plus what resumes
      where on return. That line is said only when every point above holds; until then the machine is
      not safe to close. Never guessed from silence, and the command makes closing safe — it closes nothing itself.
    - **Live status, any seat (SPEC INV-71)** — where we are NOW (the work in hand and its step)
      and what is NEXT stays answerable at a glance, kept current in the chat — the one surface every
      seat shows [INV-67]. Do not rely on the harness's own task list or spinner for this. A
      browser-seated session never shows them, and even locally they stop updating through a long
      run of tool calls. So refresh a short NOW/NEXT line at every step change, and let the heartbeat
      carry it through a long stretch. The harness task panel, where the seat shows it, is kept in plain
      product words as a courtesy (rule 6), never the status's home. On a local seat, a rendered

      live-spec runs, regardless of host.

    line is chat, lighter than a report: no pre-report walk, and no questions (SPEC INV-31). That walk
    scopes to movement-end and milestone reports, deliberately. Every law of human-facing lines still

    "(self)" stay a separate register the human may skip. Narration is for the human, and it replaces no
    report: milestones still get the full one.

    that reached its planned outcome or genuinely changed the plan — the "change of direction" this
    rule already names. A discarded attempt on the way there — a design tried and dropped, a retry, a
    false start — is not itself a beat: it folds into the eventual digest's own "why" ("three designs
    measured nothing before the fourth did"), the same way a worker's failed sub-attempt folds into
    its brief's finished answer. Worked failure: a cost measurement ran three failed instrument
    designs before one of them measured anything, and each failure was narrated as it happened,
    costing more in chat than the work itself cost in time. Two things still force a live line even

116	
117	    The requirements-format spec states this pack's three laws and their net in ONE sentence
118	    now — "declare this pack's three laws — <law>, <law>, and <law> — each naming its
119	    mechanical gate" — rather than the old separate per-law colon list naming a distinct
120	    backtick script per law. The net (mechanical gate / prover / design review) is the same
121	    one Requirement 55 names as the three enforcement kinds, so it is read once here and
122	    applied to every enumerated law, matching what the sentence itself states."""
123	    m = re.search(
124	        r"declare this pack's \w+ laws —(.+?)— each naming (?:its|a) ([a-z][a-z ]*?)[.,]",
125	        spec_flat,
126	    )
127	    if not m:
128	        return 0, []
129	    region, net_phrase = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()
130	    tok = NET_TOKEN.search(net_phrase)
131	    net = tok.group(0) if tok else None
132	    items = [

134	        for seg in region.split(",")
135	        if seg.strip()
136	    ]

every surface and transition per declared law. String rows on the three homes.

import os
import re
import unittest

from conftest import ROOT, external_clone_or_skip, read_all_flat, read_flat


class TestDeclaredLaws(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_the_home_and_the_packs_own_list(self):
        spec = read_flat("PRODUCT_SPEC.md")
        self.assertIn("declared-laws home", spec)

    def test_the_prover_station(self):
        external_clone_or_skip()
        prover = read_all_flat("skills/product-prover/SKILL.md")
        self.assertIn("Declared cross-cutting laws", prover)
        self.assertIn("dated exemption", prover)
        self.assertIn("ranks as a broken invariant", prover)

    def test_the_author_habit(self):

    def test_spec_anchor_and_index(self):
        spec = read_flat("PRODUCT_SPEC.md")
        self.assertIn("[INV-101]", spec)
        self.assertIn(
            "dated exemption", spec,
            "INV-101's body criterion doesn't carry the dated-exemption phrase",
        )
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "PRODUCT_SPEC.md"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                if line.startswith("| INV-101 |"):
                    return
        self.fail("INV-101 index row missing")


class TestLawNamesItsNet(unittest.TestCase):
    """INV-150 — every declared cross-cutting law names its enforcing net; a netless law is a
    broken invariant; declaration promotes a property from the design review to the prover.
    Homes: the routing clause + INV-101 declared-laws field + the INV-101 prover station +
    spec-author's habit + the architecture ownership backstop. (Born of the tlvphotos openable-
    face miss: a law-shaped property lived only as prose on one member, never promoted into the
    declared space where the prover enumerates, 2026-07-14.)"""

        self.assertIn("[INV-150]", spec)
        self.assertIn("Declaration is the lever", spec)

        self.assertIn("watch-level", spec)

        # body already used the two as synonyms); the demand itself — every law names what fails
        # when it is broken, a netless law is a broken invariant — is unchanged.

        self.assertIn("Every declared law names the thing that fails when the law is broken", prover)

# --- the net-floor: a declared law with no net reds without the agent (INV-150) ---

NET_TOKEN = re.compile(r"`[^`]+\.(?:sh|py)`|prover|design review|mechanical gate")


def laws_without_net(laws):
    """laws: list of (law_text, net_text_or_None). Returns the law_texts naming no net.
    The per-item floor mirroring declared_law_surface_gaps in test_interface_coverage: it
    reds if any enumerated declared law lacks a net (SPEC INV-150)."""
    return [text for text, net in laws if not net]


def parse_declared_laws_and_nets(spec_flat):
    """Parse the declared-laws home. Returns (declared_law_count, laws), where the count is
    the laws enumerated in the pack's own declared-laws sentence and laws is
    [(segment, net_or_None)].

    The requirements-format spec states this pack's three laws and their net in ONE sentence
    now — "declare this pack's three laws — <law>, <law>, and <law> — each naming its
    mechanical gate" — rather than the old separate per-law colon list naming a distinct
    backtick script per law. The net (mechanical gate / prover / design review) is the same
    one Requirement 55 names as the three enforcement kinds, so it is read once here and
    applied to every enumerated law, matching what the sentence itself states."""
    m = re.search(
        r"declare this pack's \w+ laws —(.+?)— each naming (?:its|a) ([a-z][a-z ]*?)[.,]",
        spec_flat,
    )
    if not m:
        return 0, []
    region, net_phrase = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()
    tok = NET_TOKEN.search(net_phrase)
    net = tok.group(0) if tok else None
    items = [
        re.sub(r"^and\s+", "", seg.strip())
        for seg in region.split(",")
        if seg.strip()
    ]
    declared_law_count = len(items)
    laws = [(item, net) for item in items]
    return declared_law_count, laws

    """INV-150 net-floor: the declared-laws home is parsed, each listed law enumerated, and each
    asserted to name a net — a mechanical gate, the prover's station, or the design review. A
    future declared law added with no net reds here without the agent, the same shape as the
    per-item interface/coverage floors. (Born of the tlvphotos openable-face miss, 2026-07-14.)"""

    def test_missing_net_is_flagged(self):
        laws = [("register", "`guardrails/check-shipped-language.sh`"), ("clock-honesty", None)]
        self.assertEqual(laws_without_net(laws), ["clock-honesty"],
                         "a declared law naming no net must be flagged")

    def test_fully_netted_flags_nothing(self):
        laws = [("register", "`x.sh`"), ("clock-honesty", "prover")]
        self.assertEqual(laws_without_net(laws), [])

    def test_pack_declared_laws_each_name_a_net(self):
        count, laws = parse_declared_laws_and_nets(read_flat("PRODUCT_SPEC.md"))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(count, 3, "declared-laws enumeration parse failure")
        self.assertEqual(laws_without_net(laws), [],
                         "an enumerated declared law names no net (SPEC INV-150)")
        self.assertEqual(len(laws), count,
                         "declared-law count (%d) and net assignments (%d) disagree — a law has no net"
                         % (count, len(laws)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Interface tests and the layer-to-level rule — row 294 (P8+P9, anchored on INV-101).

P8: the test level follows the footprint's layer — a presentation change is asserted at browser-computed
or above, a single-module change at its module's interface, a cross-cutting law by a string/traceability
test across every surface. P9: each module's tests assert its declared INTERFACE (one interface-level row
per architecture-node block), and a cross-cutting law (the declared-laws home, INV-101) gets one test per
surface it governs.

The traceability enforcement extends in two directions, each red-proven on a synthetic fixture:
  (A) a declared law with a surface that has no test row goes red — the same shape as a spec invariant
      with no matrix row;
  (B) a module block with no interface-level row goes red — a derivation defect at the coverage walk.
The real matrix satisfies both (every node block owns an interface row; every declared law is covered),
so the suite stays green while the checks have teeth on a violation.
"""

import os
import re
import sys
import unittest

from conftest import ROOT, external_clone_or_skip, read, read_all_flat, read_flat

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "tests"))
from test_traceability import matrix_blocks  # reuse the block parser

LADDER_LEVELS = {"string", "DOM-text", "browser-computed", "pixel"}


# --- the two check functions (the traceability extension) ---

def is_interface_row(row):
    """An interface-level row asserts the node's contract: a row that pins a ladder level and cites an
    owning test, not a bare hand-note."""
    return bool(row.get("owning", "").strip()) and row.get("level") in LADDER_LEVELS


def blocks_missing_interface_row(blocks):
    """A module block (architecture node) owns at least one interface-level row. A block with none is a
    derivation defect (P9). Returns the offending node names."""
    return [node for node, rows in blocks.items()
            if not any(is_interface_row(r) for r in rows)]


def declared_law_surface_gaps(laws):
    """laws: list of {name, surfaces: set, tested: set}. A surface a declared law governs with no test row
    is a gap (P9 / INV-101). Returns (law, surface) pairs."""
    gaps = []
    for law in laws:
        for surface in sorted(law["surfaces"]):
            if surface not in law["tested"]:
                gaps.append((law["name"], surface))
    return gaps


# --- (A) red-proven synthetically, then green on the real declared laws ---

class TestDeclaredLawSurfaceCoverage(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_untested_surface_is_flagged(self):
        laws = [{"name": "register", "surfaces": {"home", "room", "card"},
                 "tested": {"home", "room"}}]  # 'card' untested
        gaps = declared_law_surface_gaps(laws)
        self.assertIn(("register", "card"), gaps, "an untested surface of a declared law must be flagged")

    def test_fully_covered_law_flags_nothing(self):
        laws = [{"name": "clock-honesty", "surfaces": {"a", "b"}, "tested": {"a", "b"}}]
        self.assertEqual(declared_law_surface_gaps(laws), [])

    def test_pack_declared_laws_each_have_a_covering_test(self):
        """The pack's three declared laws (INV-101) are each covered by a matrix row."""
        matrix = read("TEST_MATRIX.md")
        # register on every human-facing surface [INV-28, INV-34, INV-83], clock-honest stamps [INV-24],
        # no self-certification [INV-94] — the declared-laws home names these.
        for law_anchor in ("INV-28", "INV-34", "INV-83", "INV-24", "INV-94"):
            self.assertIn(law_anchor, matrix,
                          "declared-law anchor %s has no covering matrix row" % law_anchor)


# --- (B) red-proven synthetically, then green on the real matrix ---

class TestModuleInterfaceRow(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_block_without_interface_row_is_flagged(self):
        blocks = {"good": [{"owning": "`test_x`", "level": "string"}],
                  "bad-empty": [],
                  "bad-note-only": [{"owning": "", "level": "n/a"}]}
        missing = blocks_missing_interface_row(blocks)
        self.assertIn("bad-empty", missing)
        self.assertIn("bad-note-only", missing)
        self.assertNotIn("good", missing)

    def test_every_real_node_block_owns_an_interface_row(self):
        self.assertEqual(blocks_missing_interface_row(matrix_blocks()), [],
                         "an architecture node block owns no interface-level row (P9 derivation defect)")


class TestLayerToLevelAndInterfaceLaw(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_test_author_states_the_layer_to_level_rule(self):
        ta = read_flat("skills/test-author/SKILL.md")
        self.assertIn("the test level follows the layer the change touches", ta)
        for needle in ("presentation change is asserted at browser-computed",
                       "single-module change is asserted at its module's interface",
                       "a cross-cutting law"):
            self.assertIn(needle, ta, "test-author lost the layer-to-level rule: %s" % needle)

    def test_test_author_states_the_interface_test_requirement(self):
        ta = read_flat("skills/test-author/SKILL.md")
        for needle in ("each module's tests assert its declared interface",
                       "one interface-level row per architecture-node block",
                       "one test per surface it governs"):
            self.assertIn(needle, ta, "test-author lost the interface-test requirement: %s" % needle)

    def test_coverage_checklist_gains_both(self):
        ta = read_flat("skills/test-author/SKILL.md")
        tmpl = read_flat("templates/TEST_MATRIX.template.md")
        for body, home in ((ta, "test-author"), (tmpl, "matrix template")):
            self.assertIn("interface-level row", body, "%s coverage checklist lost the interface rule" % home)
            self.assertIn("layer", body, "%s coverage checklist lost the layer-to-level rule" % home)

    def test_prover_declared_laws_station_owns_the_per_surface_test_duty(self):
        # the canon states the duty as the declared-laws sweep's second demand ("A test per
        # surface."); the INV-101 anchor is a pack fact carried by the pack adapter's pin map.
        pack = read_flat("skills/product-prover-pack/SKILL.md")
        self.assertIn("INV-101", pack)
        # The tracked-adapter anchor above holds on a bare checkout; only the canon read below needs the clone.
        external_clone_or_skip()
        pv = read_all_flat("skills/product-prover/SKILL.md")
        self.assertIn("A test per surface", pv,
                      "product-prover's declared-laws station lost the per-surface-test duty")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

## CROSS-LINK Review — INV-316, INV-317, INV-318

### 1. Procedure followed

The installed `skills/product-prover/SKILL.md` does not exist in this worktree (it's an external skill, "not tracked by this repository" per `skills/product-prover-pack/SKILL.md:79`). The pack's own maintained copy of the prover's body lives at `editions/product-prover/SKILL.md` (v1.2.0-standalone) plus `editions/product-prover/reference/stress-lenses.md` — I read both in full and ran the review against that text, cross-checked against the pack's binding page `skills/product-prover-pack/SKILL.md`.

Mode run: **New-surface review** (pipeline name `CROSS-LINK`, per the pack's own mode-name table). Per the skill's own words, this mode runs:
- Phases 1–2 (the model + structural issues), scoped to the three anchors' seams.
- The five **mandatory sweeps** of Phase 3e, each owing a verdict line: **declared cross-cutting laws**, **edge-condition completeness**, **cross-surface policy uniformity**, **unwritten seams**, and the lifecycle sweep's **paired-transition symmetry** sub-question alone (its other angles stand down in this mode).
- The two named **imaginative probes** (interactive overlap across layers; delivery separability along a declared axis) — no verdict owed.
- The whole-document **quantifier re-verify** ("sweep the document for enumerations and universal quantifiers... re-verify each such sentence against the surface set that now includes the newcomer").
- The **class lens**, standing beside the probes, closing with one class-line verdict.

### 2. Verdict per anchor

**INV-316 (R275 case 7–8) — DEFECT.**
The vendoring fix itself is real: `adopt/install-ratchet.sh:61-72` and its embedded Python `VENDOR_FILES` list (lines 117-129) both correctly add `scripts/preshow-lint.py`, `scripts/preshow-register-lint.py`, `scripts/preshow-legibility-lint.py`, and `TestRatchetInstall.test_ratchet_install_seeds_at_current_size` (`tests/test_ratchet_kit.py`) genuinely installs and hashes them end-to-end in a scratch host repo — passes.

But the **class lens** ("does the same kind live elsewhere?") catches an incomplete sweep. R275.7 states a universal rule — *any* skill-body instruction naming a run path is a class member, "vendored to every host, or naming its own absent-tool behavior." Grepping every `skills/*/SKILL.md` for script/guardrails paths turns up several more instances that are neither vendored to hosts nor carry an absent-tool sentence: `skills/spec-author/SKILL.md:197` (`scripts/build-index.py` — notably, three lines later the same file *does* state an absent-tool clause for template paths in a standalone install, proving the author knows how to write one and simply didn't here), `skills/test-author/SKILL.md:72` (`scripts/build-matrix-reference.py`, `guardrails/check-matrix-reference.py`), `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md:150/224/572` (`scripts/open-lane.sh`, `guardrails/check-authority-anchor.py`, `scripts/session-extract.py`). None of these appear in `install.sh` (skills only), `adopt/install-ratchet.sh`, or `adopt/install-scaffold.sh` (four unrelated checks).
More importantly: `tests/test_installed_copy_staleness_class.py:83-96` is a **closed, hardcoded string check** for exactly those three filenames — there is no mechanical sweep that walks every `SKILL.md` for run-path instructions and checks each against the vendored set. So R275's own criterion 1 promise ("each member naming the mechanical net that tells its running copy stale") isn't actually discharged for this new member: nothing catches the sibling instances above, and nothing would catch a sixth one landing tomorrow. The fix closes one found case; it doesn't close the class.

**INV-317 (R311) — CLEAN.**
Architecture ownership is genuinely clean: sole-owned by `base-rulebook` (`ARCHITECTURE.md:70`, pin at `ARCHITECTURE.md:91`), no second claim anywhere. `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md:587-596` (rule 36) matches the spec text closely, including the worked-failure example. `M-547` in `TEST_MATRIX.md:202` cites `tests/test_dialog_announce_law.py`, which exists and passes (7 tests). No contradicting prior text elsewhere in the pack (no other skill mentions dialogs/keychain). Edge-condition sweep: the law is explicitly scoped to a command "known" to raise a dialog; an unknown/surprise dialog is left silent, but this reads as a reasonable, non-blocking gap rather than a defect — nothing else in the pack claims completeness here.

**INV-318 (R312) — DEFECT (architecture ownership).**
Spec text is faithfully carried: `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md:598-609` (rule 37) *substantively states* the four thrift moves almost verbatim to R312.1–4, and `skills/communicator/SKILL.md:143-152` (rule 13's amendment) substantively states the beat-vs-discarded-attempt boundary (R312.5–6). Both test files exist and pass.

But `ARCHITECTURE.md` declares the *whole* anchor sole-owned by `communicator` (`ARCHITECTURE.md:217`), with an explicit note barring base-rulebook from any share: "notes — INV-318: stated in prose here as rule 37's cross-reference; owned by the communicator node, never a second ownership" (`ARCHITECTURE.md:94`). That characterization is false on its own evidence — rule 37 is not a cross-reference for the four moves, it's their substantive statement (ARCHITECTURE.md's own pin line at `line 92` even concedes this: "rule 37 — the four thrift moves"). Meanwhile communicator's own pin for INV-318 (`ARCHITECTURE.md:228`) is scoped only to "rule 13's amendment... the beat-versus-discarded-attempt boundary" — it does not claim the four-moves content at all. So the fact "the four thrift moves" is pinned to base-rulebook but owned by neither node in the ownership table (communicator's claim doesn't cover it; base-rulebook is explicitly denied it). This isn't the double-ownership the author checked for — it's the opposite failure, an orphaned fact, and it violates the architecture lens's own first check ("every fact... owned by exactly one node"). The pack's own established pattern (e.g. the `E-31` treatment at `ARCHITECTURE.md:64`) is to split ownership by sub-fact across nodes when a requirement's content genuinely splits by file; INV-318 should have gotten the same treatment instead of a blanket single-owner disclaimer.

### 3. Class-wide finding

All three anchors are individually well-tested and each has a real, working commit behind it — the author did not fabricate coverage. The pattern across all three is that **the review record was never actually run**: no `docs/prover/` file mentions INV-316/317/318 at all, despite the pack's own SKILL.md requiring this pass whenever new criteria are cross-linked to existing law. Both real defects found (the ownership mismatch on INV-318, and the stale "four members" count) are exactly the class of miss a first-pass author makes when they verify their own new text in isolation without re-reading it against what already sits beside it — the quantifier re-verify and the architecture lens both exist specifically to catch that blind spot, and neither was applied here before now.

Concretely, the quantifier re-verify also caught a second, independent defect I should flag under INV-316 (a "member list that now excludes the newcomer"): `TEST_MATRIX.md:494` (M-546, new) correctly calls the skill-body-instruction addition "**a fifth class member**," but `TEST_MATRIX.md:493` (M-336, pre-existing, untouched by this landing per `git show a67019c`) still reads "**four members**" and enumerates exactly four by name. The two rows now directly contradict each other on the class's cardinality — a `direct-contradiction` finding, cheap to fix (one word and a fifth bullet in M-336), but real and mechanically checkable, and no existing test catches it (`test_installed_copy_class_enumerates_every_member` only checks that the four named phrases are present, not that the stated count is exhaustive).

### 4. Test files

All three exist and all pass:

```
python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_installed_copy_staleness_class.py tests/test_dialog_announce_law.py tests/test_thrift_discipline.py
..................                                                       [100%]
18 passed in 0.17s
```

(`TestRatchetInstall.test_ratchet_install_seeds_at_current_size`, cited by M-546 but living in `tests/test_ratchet_kit.py`, also passes independently — 1 passed.)

### 5. Overall verdict: **RED**

Three real defects, none catastrophic but all genuine:
1. `TEST_MATRIX.md:493` (M-336) states a stale, contradicted member count ("four members") after M-546 adds a fifth — direct textual contradiction, quantifier re-verify catch.
2. `ARCHITECTURE.md:94` / `ARCHITECTURE.md:217-228` misattribute INV-318's ownership: the four-moves fact is pinned to base-rulebook (rule 37) but owned by no node in the ownership table — architecture-lens fact-ownership violation, not the double-ownership shape that was checked for and cleared.
3. INV-316's fix is real but narrow: the class-membership law it declares is universal, several sibling instances in `spec-author`, `test-author`, and `live-spec-base` remain unaddressed, and no mechanical sweep exists (only a hardcoded 3-file string check) to catch the known siblings or any future one — the class's own "mechanical net" promise isn't actually discharged for this member.

None of these are fabricated coverage or broken tests — the suite is green and the vendoring genuinely works. But per the prover's own bar ("a claim the document makes is false, or an invariant the document owes is missing" blocks), all three qualify as defects that should be applied before this lands clean.
